No name is drawn on the row: a map's name tells a reader nothing the gradient under the panel does not, and four of them turn a band of colour into a band of text.

Every panel of this row is autolevelled, because an attempt is not finished at the render: the operator measures the picture's tone and, where it sits outside the band, pushes a curve through the map's own stops and draws again. alt: Animated: three starting points advancing in step across the complex plane, one escaping fast, one bounded, one lingering near the boundary, with a |z|-versus-step chart alongside.
caption: Three orbits under the same quadratic rule, stepping together. One is past |z| = 2 within a few steps and gone for good, one stays bounded forever, and one hangs near the boundary for dozens of steps before it escapes. For the escaping tracks, the step where a track crosses the line on the chart is that orbit's escape time.
provenance: Drawn, not rendered: `python -m builder diagram escape-orbit-race`, from builder/diagrams.py. A 41-frame APNG at 960x540 (drawn at scale 2, 130 ms a frame, 1600 ms hold), plotting z <- z^2 + c from z = 0 over 40 steps at |z| > 2 for three constants: c = 0.5 + 0.5i (escapes at step 5), c = -0.075 + 0.655i (escapes at step 35), and c = -0.12256116687665 + 0.74486176661974i (never escapes). Plane panel spans +/-2.45 on both axes; the chart's ceiling is |z| = 2.5. No engine render.

alt: One Julia location under a cyclic amber palette at one, two, three and four sweeps of the gradient, each panel over a strip of the gradient repeated as many times as that panel spends it.
caption: One location and one cyclic palette, swept across the frame's range k times. At k = 1 the gradient is spent once over a range most of the frame does not occupy, and wide areas come out nearly flat; each further sweep spends it again and pulls more of the structure apart. Repetition is the classic escape from a squeezed range, and it is why so many older Mandelbrot renders are striped with rings.
provenance: scratch/render_fund/figures2.py cyclic_repeats() — four panels at 640x360, supersample 3, one location and one cyclic palette swept k times. The frame is candidate ledger key 0daf678f61143941, seat 336 of the recorded tentative gallery 20260902T161757Z: the location as it ships, addressed by its own key rather than by a position in anything. The **map is this figure's own** and not that seat's *(Matt, 2026-09-02)*: Ember Gradient, an authored map, replacing the extracted nova-25 the seat ships with. It is the same map the second column of `render-discrete-and-smooth` is drawn in, which is the one place this page repeats a palette and is Matt's own call: the two figures are four screens apart and the one a reader has already met is the one that teaches what a ramp is. nova-25 closes by *mirroring* — colour(t) equals colour(1-t) exactly, measured 0.000 — so one sweep of it is already two mirrored halves and k sweeps read as 2k bands, which is the one thing this figure must not do. An authored map closes by travelling a loop instead: 90% of the library's extracted maps are palindromes and not one of its 375 authored maps is, while every map the library calls cyclic closes exactly, so the seam a repeat could show is never the thing being traded away. Nothing replays the ledger's own cap of 6,698 — the panels are drawn at the engine's depth policy, which answers the same number at this frame. Under each panel, 6px below it and 26px tall, the gradient as that panel spends it: `fractal-wallpapers palettes strip` for the map at width 640/k, laid down k times across the panel's width. The strip command takes no cycle count, so the repeat is composed from k engine-drawn ramps rather than one stretched — the map is cyclic and so drawn unfolded, which is the mirror false the renders above carry.

alt: A row of five plates: find locations, the location pool, find wallpapers, the candidate pool, curate a gallery, with arrows running left to right between them. Under the last plate is the solve's shortfall readout, and one heavier arrow runs out of it, back along its own lane and up into find wallpapers.
caption: The three parts, and the two stores between them. Locations accumulate in one pool and judged pictures in the other, and neither is ever pruned. The arrow back is what makes this a loop rather than a sequence: what the solve could not seat is what the next mine reads.
provenance: Drawn, not rendered: `python -m builder diagram pipeline-overview`, from builder/diagrams.py. A PNG at 1316x418 on the stylesheet's own well, composed at the width every figure of this article is composed at. No engine render and no record read — the figure's subject is the shape of the loop, which is the one thing on this page that no record holds. The wording of every box is this page's own prose reduced to two or three lines, and nothing on it is a count.

Five plates in one row: the three parts, with a store drawn between each pair and narrower than a part, because a store holds rather than does. The shortfall readout hangs under the solve that writes it and stops at the second store's left edge, so the lane the return arrow climbs is clear of it — an arrow crossing a plate it has nothing to do with is a line a reader has to work out rather than read.

The return arrow is the spine's own ink a rank heavier rather than a colour of its own: it is the one line of the figure a reader is asked to follow, and a fourth ink would be a fourth thing to learn. Every line of lettering is held to fitting inside the box that carries it, and an overrun is a refusal rather than words running out over the well.

The last diagram of this kind on the site. Its sibling on finding-good-wallpapers.html — the same three parts drawn as the material each one hands on — was replaced on 2026-09-05 by wallpapers-three-bands, which makes that claim out of real pictures, so the flow-box helpers in builder/diagrams.py now have one caller. What is drawn here is the loop, and the arrow that runs backwards is the whole of why it is still a diagram.

alt: A stacked area chart of admissions per batch over one run of the search, smoothed, with one band per partition and a legend naming the nine. The stack falls steeply through the first half of the run and runs low and spiky to the end; under the axis, four brackets give the raw admissions per batch over each quarter of the run.
caption: How a run's yield falls as it goes. The first quarter of this run admitted roughly eight times as much per batch as the last, and the stack says which partitions the later admissions came from. The remedy for that tail is new ground rather than a different split of the batches.
provenance: Drawn, not rendered: a chart composed by builder.pipeline:yield_decay from artifacts/harvest_run10/walk.jsonl — 109,553 ledger rows read streamed, of which 5,279 are admissions. Nothing is rendered and no engine is reached.

It stopped on active-time budget after 1,681 batches and 317 active minutes. Its channels were contest, share — the proven channel was off, which is what the HTML comment beside this figure's block is about.

An admission is a `candidate` row whose fate is `survived`; a row's partition is derived from its family by builder.pipeline:partition_of, and the nine derived totals are held to the run's own summary tally before anything is drawn.

The curve is a centred moving average of admissions per batch over 81 batches, the window shortened rather than zero-padded at either end. The brackets under the axis are the raw count over each quarter, which is what the caption's ratio is taken on.

alt: Two line charts sharing one logarithmic axis of mining effort, in attempts, from about three thousand to about a hundred and seventy-seven thousand. The upper chart plots the median ranking score of the seated gallery; the lower plots the tenth percentile of the same seats. Each carries one line per gallery size — fifty, one hundred, two hundred — with a band around it showing the spread of three random draws. Every line rises from left to right, and the smaller galleries sit above the larger ones throughout.
caption: The candidate pool re-solved over random fractions of the mining that made it, three draws at each fraction and three gallery sizes. Seats stop being bought early: fifty seats fill at every fraction measured, and two hundred from a quarter of the mining upward. Quality keeps being bought at every doubling so far, and the weakest seats gain the most of it. A hollow marker is a fraction whose draws could not fill the gallery.
provenance: Drawn, not rendered: a chart composed by builder.growth:what_more_mining_buys from growth.jsonl of the curation growth run 20260902T150756Z — artifacts/curation/growth/20260902T150756Z/, 76 rows, taken at 2026-09-02T15:27:05Z against wallpapers commit b5ce263301b7.
